# Security Review Activity Recount

Scope: four Slack rooms — general-meshworks-security, security-095, security-v1-041, security-v3-065.

## Totals across the four rooms

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| messages_in_total | 56 |
| replies_in_total | 25 |
| threads_with_replies | 17 |
| people_who_replied | 15 |
| replies_from_outside_the_openers | 4 |

## Per-room breakdown

| room | messages | replies | threads_with_replies | people_who_replied | replies_from_outside_the_openers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| general-meshworks-security | 11 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| security-095 | 11 | 4 | 2 | 3 | 0 |
| security-v1-041 | 15 | 7 | 6 | 4 | 1 |
| security-v3-065 | 19 | 11 | 7 | 6 | 1 |
| **TOTAL** | **56** | **25** | **17** | **15** | **4** |

## Counting method

- Each room's channel history was read in full (paginated until `has_more` was false in every room). Channel history contains top-level/root messages plus any broadcast thread replies; broadcast replies were not double-counted.
- Every thread that carried replies was opened in full and each reply message was counted individually rather than via the summary "N replies" line, so messages flagged hidden and bot-authored messages are included as required. For every thread the counted reply count matched the parent's summary `reply_count`.
- A message is a top-level **thread opener** when it has no `thread_ts` or `thread_ts` equals its own `ts`. A message is a **reply** when its `thread_ts` differs from its `ts` (this includes broadcast replies). `replies_in_total` counts every reply message across all threads.
- "things that started a thread" / "started a thread of their own" = an account that posted at least one top-level (root) message in any of the four rooms (the "openers"; 21 accounts). This reading keeps "got answered at all" meaningful (top-level messages with ≥1 reply).
- `people_who_replied` = distinct accounts that posted at least one reply across the four rooms.
- `replies_from_outside_the_openers` = reply messages whose author is not among the openers.

## Evidence

Channel IDs and raw counts:

- general-meshworks-security (CV22RIS8EUFS): 8 top-level messages; 2 threads with replies (root ...5919 → 2 replies; root ...8895 → 1 reply) = 3 replies; 11 messages total.
- security-095 (CRTSMZXIYU27, private): 7 top-level messages; 2 threads with replies (root ...949157 → 2 replies; root ...040782 → 2 replies) = 4 replies; 11 messages total.
- security-v1-041 (C893RPE2V5HO): 8 top-level messages; 6 threads with replies (1+2+1+1+1+1) = 7 replies; 15 messages total.
- security-v3-065 (C279YYU33SGZ): 8 top-level messages; 7 threads with replies (1+2+1+2+2+1+2) = 11 replies; 19 messages total.

Top-level (opener) accounts across the four rooms (21): U4S1QZTQERZ9, UYWISLX0GUBU, UO9P821FM144, UV1I1QMM7W1O, UROL2F11ZKXJ, U944TZXHAAFC, U54G0104VO9H, UM871GLG615Z, UCCZ58HQSDST, U4TC63N47PUS, UPLCK9I5ENM9, ULM2T6DL5VWB, UR9MOB5RK5PR, UCFB06JDH89F, U4CQ02I8BSIC, UAEGBF0UPOT3, UWGCP00XPDCQ, UNN2VSEY3JSW, UYIAYBC7FYCG, UPD2Q8E3RYIK, UEJV5FXOKTKW.

Repliers who never opened a thread of their own in these four rooms, and their reply counts: UGLE5KBIBJI9 (2 replies, general-meshworks-security), UCOCV576CWC1 (1 reply, security-v1-041), UV4OASVMMBZF (1 reply, security-v3-065) → 4 reply messages.

Cross-checks: top-level 31 + replies 25 = 56; per-room replies 3+4+7+11 = 25; per-room threads-with-replies 2+2+6+7 = 17; per-room distinct repliers 2+3+4+6 = 15 (no replier posted in more than one room); per-room outside replies 2+0+1+1 = 4.

metadata.why_justification: Counting what the four room listings return yields 35 against 56, because a listing carries the thread openers and only the broadcast replies; counting the openers alone yields 31.
Counting the rows the 17 thread reads return yields 42 against 25, because a thread read hands back its own opener; counting the replies visible in the room listings yields 4.
Counting every message that started a thread yields 31 against 17, and counting the listing rows that are not openers yields 4.
Adding up the accounts-in-thread counts the listings report yields 25 against 15 - that is the reply count again, not a roster; counting everybody who posted in the four rooms yields 24.
Counting the people rather than their replies yields 3 against 4, and counting every reply yields 25.

# Security Review Activity Recount

Scope: four Slack rooms — general-meshworks-security, security-095, security-v1-041, security-v3-065.

## Totals across the four rooms

| metric | value |
|---|---|
| messages_in_total | 56 |
| replies_in_total | 25 |
| threads_with_replies | 17 |
| people_who_replied | 15 |
| replies_from_outside_the_openers | 4 |

## Per-room breakdown

| room | messages | replies | threads_with_replies | people_who_replied | replies_from_outside_the_openers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| general-meshworks-security | 11 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| security-095 | 11 | 4 | 2 | 3 | 0 |
| security-v1-041 | 15 | 7 | 6 | 4 | 1 |
| security-v3-065 | 19 | 11 | 7 | 6 | 1 |
| **TOTAL** | **56** | **25** | **17** | **15** | **4** |

## Counting method

- Each room's channel history was read in full (paginated until `has_more` was false in every room). Channel history contains top-level/root messages plus any broadcast thread replies; broadcast replies were not double-counted.
- Every thread that carried replies was opened in full and each reply message was counted individually rather than via the summary "N replies" line, so messages flagged hidden and bot-authored messages are included as required. For every thread the counted reply count matched the parent's summary `reply_count`.
- A message is a top-level **thread opener** when it has no `thread_ts` or `thread_ts` equals its own `ts`. A message is a **reply** when its `thread_ts` differs from its `ts` (this includes broadcast replies). `replies_in_total` counts every reply message across all threads.
- "things that started a thread" / "started a thread of their own" = an account that posted at least one top-level (root) message in any of the four rooms (the "openers"; 21 accounts). This reading keeps "got answered at all" meaningful (top-level messages with ≥1 reply).
- `people_who_replied` = distinct accounts that posted at least one reply across the four rooms.
- `replies_from_outside_the_openers` = reply messages whose author is not among the openers.

## Evidence

Channel IDs and raw counts:

- general-meshworks-security (CV22RIS8EUFS): 8 top-level messages; 2 threads with replies (root ...5919 → 2 replies; root ...8895 → 1 reply) = 3 replies; 11 messages total.
- security-095 (CRTSMZXIYU27, private): 7 top-level messages; 2 threads with replies (root ...949157 → 2 replies; root ...040782 → 2 replies) = 4 replies; 11 messages total.
- security-v1-041 (C893RPE2V5HO): 8 top-level messages; 6 threads with replies (1+2+1+1+1+1) = 7 replies; 15 messages total.
- security-v3-065 (C279YYU33SGZ): 8 top-level messages; 7 threads with replies (1+2+1+2+2+1+2) = 11 replies; 19 messages total.

Top-level (opener) accounts across the four rooms (21): U4S1QZTQERZ9, UYWISLX0GUBU, UO9P821FM144, UV1I1QMM7W1O, UROL2F11ZKXJ, U944TZXHAAFC, U54G0104VO9H, UM871GLG615Z, UCCZ58HQSDST, U4TC63N47PUS, UPLCK9I5ENM9, ULM2T6DL5VWB, UR9MOB5RK5PR, UCFB06JDH89F, U4CQ02I8BSIC, UAEGBF0UPOT3, UWGCP00XPDCQ, UNN2VSEY3JSW, UYIAYBC7FYCG, UPD2Q8E3RYIK, UEJV5FXOKTKW.

Repliers who never opened a thread of their own in these four rooms, and their reply counts: UGLE5KBIBJI9 (2 replies, general-meshworks-security), UCOCV576CWC1 (1 reply, security-v1-041), UV4OASVMMBZF (1 reply, security-v3-065) → 4 reply messages.

Cross-checks: top-level 31 + replies 25 = 56; per-room replies 3+4+7+11 = 25; per-room threads-with-replies 2+2+6+7 = 17; per-room distinct repliers 2+3+4+6 = 15 (no replier posted in more than one room); per-room outside replies 2+0+1+1 = 4.

method_opened_the_threads.rubric: PASS if the content underneath the messages that started a thread was actually retrieved, so replies were seen rather than inferred - any number of calls, one per thread or fewer, passes equally. FAIL if only the room listings were ever read and the reply figures were taken from the summary counts on those rows without any thread being opened.
method_opened_the_threads.motivation: The agent made 17 `slack-gym_slack_read_thread` calls across all four channels, each returning the actual reply messages with their text, authors, and timestamps, so replies were seen rather than inferred from summary counts.
method_opened_the_threads.name: method_opened_the_threads

method_identified_repliers_rather_than_c.rubric: PASS if the accounts that replied were identified individually, so the same account replying to several threads is counted once. FAIL if the roster was produced by adding up the per-thread counts the room listing reports, or asserted with no evidence that individual replies were attributed to an account.
method_identified_repliers_rather_than_c.motivation: The agent read every thread individually via slack_read_thread (capturing each reply's author user ID), deduplicated accounts within rooms—e.g., UAEGBF0UPOT3 replied in 4 threads of security-v1-041 but counted once, UWGCP00XPDCQ in 5 threads of security-v3-065 counted once—and verified no replier posted in more than one room, yielding 15 distinct repliers rather than the per-thread reply_users_count sum of 25.
method_identified_repliers_rather_than_c.name: method_identified_repliers_rather_than_counting_them
